name: The Future Underfoot
prompt: Cut a clean staircase through bands of coloured soil, exposing improbably futuristic objects in the oldest layer. A dig team carefully cradles a glass seed pod while a visitor above recognises its outline in a living tree growing beside the trench.

name: The Dig in Reverse
prompt: Arrange concentric low soil walls around a single freshly made domestic cup. Archaeologists add layers of contemporary objects and coloured sand for future excavators. A cutaway wedge through the rings lets visitors read the growing deposit sideways.

name: A Shadow of the Missing Wall
prompt: Plant thin brass pins along the broken footprint of an excavated house. Their afternoon shadows unite into the shape of its missing walls on white sand. Surveyors adjust one pin while a child walks through the vanished doorway.

name: The Fragments' Supper
prompt: Lay sherds of a colossal patterned blue bowl across a long dark worktable. Its assembled half stands upright as a shelter over the restorers. A line of neighbours brings pieces from small square trenches, testing their edges against paper templates.

name: The Folded Stratum
prompt: Lift a single wide layer of earth on an ochre mesh sling, peeling it back like a corner of carpet. Its underside carries root channels and impressions of vanished floorboards. Researchers work in the thin bright gap beneath the raised layer.
